slides.title:
6 SEO fixes
for category
pages
slides.accentLine: Most stores skip at least one.

slides.title: Link to every
slides.body: Google finds products by following links. If a category page skips some, Googlebot might never find them.
slides.action: Make sure each category page (incl. page 2, 3…) links to all of its products.
slides.example: “Running shoes” links to all 48 shoes, not just the 12 bestsellers.

slides.title: Real links,
slides.body: Google can only follow real HTML links: an a tag with an href. A JavaScript-only “Load more” can hide products.
slides.action: Right-click a product link → Inspect. It should be an a tag with href="/product-url".
slides.example: Keep the “Load more” button, but add plain page links underneath it.

slides.title: Every page gets
slides.body: Google treats page 2, 3 and 4 as separate pages. It ignores anything after a #, so #page=2 isn’t a page.
slides.action: Use ?page=2 style URLs. Don’t set page 1 as the canonical for every page.
slides.example: /running-shoes?page=2 has a canonical pointing to itself.

slides.title: Tame your
slides.body: Size, colour and price filters can create thousands of near-identical URLs that waste Google’s crawl time.
slides.action: Block filter combos nobody searches for in robots.txt. Return a 404 for empty results.
slides.example: Crawl /running-shoes/women. Block sorted or stacked filter URLs like ?sort=price.

slides.title: A unique title
slides.body: Duplicate or vague titles are one reason Google may rewrite the blue link it shows for your page.
slides.action: Put the category name first and make every category title different.
slides.example: “Women’s Trail Running Shoes | Store Name”, not “Shop – Page 1”.

slides.title: Breadcrumbs
slides.body: Breadcrumbs show Google how your categories connect. BreadcrumbList markup can show that path in results.
slides.action: Add a visible breadcrumb trail plus BreadcrumbList structured data.
